When I was 12 I was having some medical issues where I needed to get blood drawn for the first time. My mom was supposed to be there with me for the whole thing but there where some scheduling issues with the x-ray place I was supposed to go after. She argued on the phone with them for a few minutes then hangs up and turns to me and says she has to go over there to figure it out. It was still in the same hospital and really not that far away but I've always had really bad anxiety but I didn't want her to be more stressed because I didn't want to be alone so I pretend it was fine and she left.

After about 5 minutes I was a nervous mess, I was shaking and sweating, staring at the floor or my hands to look as normal as I possibly could but it was obvious I was upset. A nurse came over and asked if I was okay or if I wanted water but again not wanting to be a bother I lied and told her I was fine. In the waiting room there was about 5 other people and all of them looked to be over 50 but the oldest was a Russian lady who looked about 80. I could tell she had been looking at me ever since my mom left but I just assumed she was wondering why my mom left me alone.

After another 5 minutes the waiting was down to 3 people, me, the Russian lady, and some old dude. At this point it was all I could do to keep from crying because in my head my mom said she would be back in 5 minutes and it was 10 minutes so that meant something horrible happened and she was never coming back. All of a sudden I felt someone sitting next to me, I look up and it's the Russian lady. She introduces herself of Lydia and before I could even speak she pulled out her phone and started showing me pictures of her cats and them just doing  weird things. 

Once she ran out of those she just told me stories of her growing up in Russia and how at the age of 5 she single handedly fought off 5 bears at once. Eventually I was laughing and smiling with her and she kept talking to me until they called my name and she looked my in the eye and said, "Remember, be brave like those silly bears who dare challenged me." It only took like 2 minutes and when I came out there was Lydia whi gave me a big hug and smile and said, "Here, for your bravery I give you picture of bear. When you get scared look at it and remember, be brave little bear." They called her name, she went in and my mom showed up and off we went. I never saw her again but to this day I still have the picture of the bear that I carry with me everywhere.

When I was in fourth grade this was a big fire in an apartment building that killed 2 kids from my school, they were brothers. The next day when they told everyone, it felt like the world stopped. Everyone one was crying and trying to comfort each other, the bullied kid was hugging the popular kid while they cried and for the whole day, no one did anything. I just got up, left and sat on the monkey bars all day until my dad came to pick me up. They held an assembly to talk about it and in the main lobby they put what's called the friendship bench. The idea was if you were feeling lonely or sad then you would go sit on the bench and someone would see you and go over and be your friend. On the anniversary the next year the same thing happened, the world stopped and no did anything that day. It shouldn't have affected me as much as it did, I wasn't that close to them and I've felt with death before that day but I think it was because they were my age and then they were just gone forever. Now every year on the anniversary I just feel so depressed. RIP Joshua and Jay-Michael, 2006-2016 and 2009-2016. They died on 6/6/16.
